correctness.rationale: A fresh exhaustive reconstruction over all \(6^3=216\) strict balanced \(3\times3\) profiles reproduced exactly 54 serial-dictatorship failures, with rank-maximal-set sizes 36 singleton and 18 doubleton. It also reproduced the claimed six rank-signature transitions (multiplicities 24 and five times 6) and exactly nine object-relabeling classes, each of size six. A separate direct check of all four \(2\times2\) profiles shows no failure, so three agents/objects is the first balanced size. The rank-maximal comparator was computed from the lexicographically maximal rank-count signature over all bijections, matching the primary definition.
risks: The theorem is for a fixed serial priority order, strict complete preferences, and balanced markets.
sources: Fresh exhaustive enumeration of the complete 216-profile universe

evidence: Irving et al. define rank-maximality by lexicographic rank signature and give algorithms; they do not compare it with serial dictatorship on the complete \(3\times3\) profile space.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies the sharp smallest balanced market where a canonical strategyproof priority mechanism ceases to be rank-maximal and completely classifies every failure at that boundary. The exact 54/216 rate, severity split and nine relabeling types are a natural structural boundary, not an arbitrary parameter slice.

limitations: No assertion is made about random priority orders, larger markets, ties, or incomplete preference lists.
